description: Cross-port numeric conformance fixtures for the arrayop runtime (ess-zmm, extended for spatial PDE stencils by ess-bdm). Executing ports must simulate each fixture and assert that every inline 'tests' assertion matches within the declared tolerance. Non-executing ports explicitly skip with a documented reason. See README.md for the skip contract and adapter notes.

fixtures.notes: Method-of-lines 1-D heat equation: a pure-map LHS-arrayop whose RHS body is index(makearray(interior + 2 Dirichlet ghost regions), i). The discretized stencil IR is the shared artifact; bindings evaluate it numerically and match the exact discrete eigenvalue solution u[i,t]=exp(lambda_1*t)*sin(pi*i/5), lambda_1=-9.5492 (rel tol 1e-3). Rust evaluates this VECTORIZED — whole-array shifted-slice stencils + region-materialized makearray, no per-cell scalarization (ess-bdm; simulate_array.rs try_eval_arrayop_vectorized, verified N-independent in tests/pde_vectorized_eval.rs). Python uses the numpy vectorized shifted-slice path (PR #25); Julia uses the tree-walk LHS-arrayop unroller (tree_walk_arrayop_test.jl testset 6).

fixtures.notes: Cumulative (prefix) reductions, esm-spec §4.3.1 — the canonical spelling of a running total is an `aggregate` whose `filter` compares the contracted index against an output index; the format ships no cumsum/scan op. All four monotone variants over one source field: inclusive/exclusive forward, inclusive reverse, and a forward running `max`. The exclusive variant's first cell reduces over the EMPTY set and pins that it takes the semiring's additive identity rather than erroring; the running max pins that the pattern is not `+`-specific — and caught a real bug, the Python bare-`reduce` shorthand seeding every fold with 0.0 instead of ⊕'s own identity, which clamped all-negative maxima to zero. Rust and Python recognize the FORWARD rows and evaluate them with an O(N) running accumulator instead of the O(N²) triangle; the rewrite is bit-identical because both fold the admitted window ascending in the same association (pinned by pkg/earthsci-ast-rs/tests/cumulative_prefix_scan.rs and pkg/earthsci-ast-py/tests/test_cumulative_prefix_scan.py). Julia evaluates the triangular form correctly but does not yet scan: its array backend unrolls a constant-bound contraction into per-cell-INDEPENDENT kernels (_unrolled_contraction_body), and a scan is sequential ACROSS output cells, which that kernel model has no slot for.

fixtures.notes: The measure-weighted counterpart of fixture 25, esm-spec §4.3.1 'a cumulative sum is not a cumulative integral'. The format carries no measure concept (§6.6.5 convention 2), so a Riemann-sum cumulative integral multiplies the per-cell measure into the body as an ordinary factor. NON-UNIFORM cell widths are the point: an unweighted prefix sum of the same field would give [0.5, 1.75, 3.375, 5.25] instead of the analytic [0.25, 0.5625, 0.765625, 1.0], so this fixture fails loudly if any binding ever supplies or infers a measure of its own. The midpoint rule is exact for the linear integrand 2x, so the assertions are equalities, not discretization-error bounds.
